title: A systematic review into the incidence, severity and duration of antidepressant withdrawal effects: Are guidelines evidence-based?
population: 24 studies of antidepressant withdrawal with diverse methods, including online surveys of antidepressant users
funder: not read: the archived publisher page shows only the abstract, the university repository returned HTTP 403, and Crossref metadata list no funder. Davies is affiliated with the All-Party Parliamentary Group for Prescribed Drug Dependence and Read with the International Institute for Psychiatric Drug Withdrawal.
result: Withdrawal incidence in 14 studies ranged from 27% to 86%, weighted average 56%. In four large studies of severity, a weighted average of 46% of those with withdrawal effects endorsed the most extreme severity rating offered. Seven of ten studies on duration found that a significant proportion had withdrawal for more than two weeks; mean durations in the four studies that calculated one were 5 days, 10 days, 43 days and 79 weeks. Results read from the abstract.
